position: A public museum of claim-boundary failures: every card maps an unsupported agent claim to the receipt a runtime contract should demand.

cases.example_violation: Claimed a commit/push without a resolving commit-hash receipt. A real push produces a SHA that `git cat-file -t` can verify. Run it and cite the actual hash from `git rev-parse HEAD`, or remove the claim.
cases.title: The Agent Said Done While The Artifact Was Still Missing
cases.buyer_failure: A coding or ops agent reports completion before the durable artifact, deploy, commit, or queue item exists.
cases.missing_receipt: artifact path, commit hash, deploy receipt, message id, or queue record
cases.control: Block final completion language unless the named artifact exists and the worktree/state agrees.
cases.audit_prompt: Find every place the agent used completion language without an independently readable artifact.

cases.example_violation: run_shell command contains 3 personal identifier(s) [categories: deny-list]. PII must not appear in shell commands that could reach third parties (email, curl POST, browser scripts).
cases.title: The Agent Tried To Put Private Identity Data Into A Tool Boundary
cases.buyer_failure: An outbound or automation agent risks leaking personal identifiers through shell commands, browser scripts, or third-party calls.
cases.missing_receipt: redaction proof and approved outbound identity context
cases.control: Enforce identity and credential separation at the client layer, not just prompt text.
cases.audit_prompt: Inspect tool calls for personal identifiers, private domains, tokens, or account-mixing risks.

minimum_payload: where the operator had to manually check
